ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Phillis Wheatley Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient visit for three months of winter wheeze, cough and breathlessness in a 19-year-old woman called asthmatic since childhood and never tested: examination, chest X-ray, blood count, tuberculosis and pregnancy tests, and planning of lung function testing; trauma-informed social history. Concerns: Her chest is worse every winter, and cough at night keeps her from sleeping and writing; She may soon travel by sea to see her book published abroad, and wants to be well enough to go; She wants her care to be her own: her consent, her information, and her decisions. [S]

tr.td: Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg inhaler as needed only (GINA track 1, step 2, anti-inflammatory reliever): one inhalation whenever needed for symptoms or before exercise in the cold, no more than 12 inhalations a day
Prednisone 20 mg oral tablet, standby course for the sea journey and the summer away: two tablets (40 mg) each morning for five days, to start only as her action plan directs
40 mg each morning for five days if the action plan directs
Meclizine 25 mg oral tablet, one tablet an hour before sailing and then once daily as needed for seasickness
One tablet daily as needed at sea

Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg inhaler as maintenance and reliever (GINA track 1, step 3): one inhalation twice daily and one inhalation as needed, no more than 12 inhalations a day
One inhalation twice daily plus one as needed

tr.td: Chest X-ray, posteroanterior and lateral: lungs clear and not hyperinflated; no consolidation, hilar enlargement, cavity, scarring or effusion; heart size normal

Spirometry before and 15 minutes after albuterol 400 mcg, with FeNO, interpreted with GLI Global race-neutral equations: FEV1 2.24 L (83 percent predicted) rising to 2.57 L (+330 mL, +15 percent); FEV1/FVC 0.72 before (below the lower limit of normal of 0.75) and 0.80 after; FeNO 38 ppb. Reversible airflow obstruction: asthma

Written asthma action plan, given and explained: green zone use the reliever as needed; yellow zone (more symptoms, waking, or peak flow below 80 percent of her best) use more reliever inhalations up to 12 a day and call the clinic; red zone (peak flow below 50 percent, cannot speak in sentences, or no relief) emergency care. Peak flow meter given; zones to be set from her personal best
Inhaler technique with her new pressurized inhaler and a spacer: taught and checked by teach-back; correct

Asthma action plan updated for travel: peak flow zones set from her personal best of 400 L/min (green above 320, yellow 200 to 320, red below 200); instructions for the standby prednisone course and for finding care at sea and abroad; a printed medical summary
Advance care planning conversation, about 16 minutes, with her consent

list.item: Wheeze, cough and breathlessness this winter, for about three months: symptoms on three or four days a week, waking with cough and a tight chest about twice a month, breathless climbing the hill streets in cold air; worse with cold wind, kitchen and fireplace smoke, and colds; called a weak chest and asthma since childhood but never tested or treated. Asthma to be confirmed with spirometry before and after bronchodilator and FeNO: resolved, confirmed [S]

Asthma, confirmed, mild persistent: variable airflow obstruction (FEV1/FVC 0.72, below the lower limit of normal, rising to 0.80 after bronchodilator; FEV1 2.24 L, 83 percent predicted, rising 330 mL or 15 percent); type 2 inflammation (FeNO 38 ppb, blood eosinophils 0.38 x10^3/uL, total IgE 165, house dust mite sensitization); tuberculosis infection test negative and chest X-ray clear. Triggers: cold air, kitchen and fireplace smoke, colds: active, confirmed [S]

Asthma exacerbation with a cold a week after returning from abroad: three days of wheeze, chest tightness and waking at night despite six to eight reliever inhalations a day; peak flow 270 L/min (68 percent of her best of 400), oxygen saturation 96 percent; 330 L/min after treatment in clinic; treated without oral corticosteroids; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]
Prone to seasickness on boat trips; meclizine for the sea crossing; resolved on her return: resolved, confirmed [S]

Pregnancy planning: not sexually active and no contraception wanted now; she may wish to have children one day; folic acid by her choice, and asthma care planned before and during any pregnancy: active, confirmed [S]

list.item: Born in West Africa; taken from her family by traffickers as a young child and brought to Boston, where she has lived since in the household of the family who acquired her. She works in the house as a domestic companion without wages, does not hold her own identity papers, and the household decides where she may travel. She knows nothing of her birth family [S]

Taught to read and write in the household; reads the Bible, Latin and Greek classics and English poetry; a published poet whose first book is being prepared for publication abroad. Writes in the early morning and late at night. Her sources of strength are her faith, her writing and her correspondence with a close friend [S]
Exposures: no tobacco, vaping, alcohol or drug use; cooks over a gas range without a vented hood and tends the wood fireplaces in the house; walks the steep streets of the old town in winter wind [S]
Not sexually active; has not been pregnant; no one pressures her about sex or pregnancy (asked privately) [S]

Seen alone for part of the visit, as every patient is; she is an adult and makes her own decisions. Asked privately, she says she is not physically harmed, and that she hopes to win her freedom in her own way; she accepted written information and the clinic social worker's direct line (555-0142), and declined other help for now. Results and plans go to her alone, and the clinic takes no instructions about her care from the household [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for three months of winter wheeze, cough and breathlessness in a 19-year-old woman called asthmatic since childhood and never tested: examination, chest X-ray, blood count, tuberculosis and pregnancy tests, and planning of lung function testing; trauma-informed social history
Diagnosis visit: spirometry with bronchodilator response and FeNO with the pulmonology consultation; asthma confirmed; start of as-needed budesonide-formoterol (GINA track 1); action plan; vaccines
Six-week asthma review: control, technique, personal best peak flow, triggers, and planning for a long sea journey and a summer away
Asthma review after an exacerbation with a cold on her return from abroad: control, repeat spirometry and FeNO, the winter plan, completion of vaccines, and her changed circumstances
Periodic preventive visit before a long sea journey
Same-day sick visit for asthma with a cold after returning from abroad

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Pulmonology consultation in two weeks with spirometry before and after bronchodilator and FeNO, to confirm or refute asthma, exclude other chest disease, and plan treatment and preparation for travel

Work-up of wheeze and cough: chest X-ray, blood count with eosinophils, interferon-gamma release assay for tuberculosis infection (born in a country where tuberculosis is common), and a urine pregnancy test before treatment; no inhaler is started before testing unless symptoms worsen

Trauma-informed, patient-centred care: seen alone for part of every visit; consent, information and results to her alone, through her own contact details; no instructions about her care accepted from the household; private screening for safety and exploitation at each visit, with resources and social work offered and her decisions respected
Equity safeguards: spirometry read with race-neutral GLI Global equations, plain explanation of every result, and attention to the higher asthma burden carried by Black women

GINA track 1, step 2: as-needed low-dose budesonide-formoterol (no albuterol-only reliever), a written action plan with peak flow zones, technique checks and trigger reduction (kitchen ventilation, avoiding fireplace smoke, a scarf in cold wind, mite-proof bedding); review six weeks after starting and within a week of any exacerbation
Vaccines for an adult with asthma: influenza and COVID-19 each season, and PCV20 once

Travel plan for a long sea journey: two inhalers and a spacer, an updated action plan, a standby five-day prednisone course with clear start rules, meclizine for seasickness, an aired cabin away from smoke, a printed medical summary and contact with the clinic by message

Contraception and pregnancy planning on her terms: information on every method (all suitable with asthma), folic acid 0.4 mg daily by her choice, and asthma review before and during any pregnancy with budesonide as the preferred inhaled steroid and the controller never stopped
After the exacerbation: GINA track 1 step 3, budesonide-formoterol one inhalation twice daily and as needed through the winter, with a step-down to as-needed treatment in the spring if she stays well
Social work, at her request, for health coverage in her own name, income and housing after she gained her freedom
A confirmed diagnosis within two weeks: spirometry with bronchodilator response and FeNO, with tuberculosis excluded
Asthma confirmed by a 330 mL (15 percent) bronchodilator response and FeNO 38 ppb; tuberculosis test negative and chest X-ray clear, two weeks after the first visit
Asthma Control Test 20 or more with no night waking
Asthma Control Test 21 and no night waking six weeks after starting treatment; 20 after the exacerbation
Correct inhaler technique and a written action plan she can use at home and at sea
Technique correct at every visit; plan used during the exacerbation
Well enough to make the sea journey and spend the summer away
Travelled and stayed well all summer without the standby prednisone
No exacerbation needing an oral corticosteroid
Achieved: one exacerbation with a cold, managed with extra budesonide-formoterol and a step-up, without prednisone
Hepatitis B and HPV vaccination complete
Hepatitis B series complete; HPV dose 3 due

list.item: Independent in all activities of daily living; this winter she stops to rest when climbing hills in the cold, and night cough leaves her tired for her writing [S]
Alert, articulate and composed; speaks with quiet precision and asks exact questions about her tests; PHQ-2 1; no thoughts of self-harm [S]
